A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PEARL, with matching core algorithms and experiments. The complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support comparison. Revised experimental settings limit direct performance comparisons, but do not prevent comparison of the documents.

before.justification: v1 reports original PEARL speedup measurements, component ablations, window-size experiments, and accepted-token measurements, although some baseline results are attributed to earlier work.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results, multilingual evaluations, component timings, forward-pass counts, and resource-competition experiments in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The core pre-verify/post-verify procedure and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. However, Section 4.5 and Appendix G introduce a substantial deployment adaptation: duplicate the draft model on the first and last GPUs, divide drafting between them, and transfer KV caches to avoid competition with the pipeline-parallel target model. Tensor-parallel integration in Appendix F remains prospective.

E1.justification: v3 retains HumanEval, GSM8K, and MT-bench, while adding MGSM evaluation in ten non-English languages. It also evaluates co-located models under resource competition, a deployment scenario absent from v1. Reporting MT-bench categories separately does not itself add task coverage.

E2.justification: Assisted Generation is added to the HumanEval, GSM8K, and MT-bench comparisons. DistillSpec, which has an MT-bench result in v1 Table 2, is removed from the evaluated comparisons. Speculative Decoding, Ouroboros, and Lookahead remain in the corresponding retained experiments.

E3.justification: Reported hardware changes from H800 GPUs to A100-SXM4-80G GPUs, and maximum generation lengths for GSM8K and MT-bench change from 512 to 256. v3 adds Llama 3.1 8B/70B configurations, MGSM sampling, resource-competition protocols, and an SD window-size search. These are reported setting changes and additions; they do not establish that every retained table was rerun.

E4.justification: v3 retains the component ablations, PEARL window-size sensitivity study, and accepted-token analysis. It adds a real-prompt execution trace, SD window-size searches, communication and computation timing breakdowns, forward-pass overhead analysis, KV-transfer latency versus input length, and extensive resource-competition tests. These substantially expand the examination of efficiency mechanisms and deployment limitations.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-trial counts, confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars. The model-run counts added in v3 Table 11 measure forward passes, not repeated experimental trials.

E6.justification: Many benchmark and throughput values change, and substantial multilingual, profiling, and resource-competition results are added. For CodeLlama 7B/70B on HumanEval, Table 1 reports PEARL/SD speedups of 3.79/2.76 in v1 and 4.43/3.03 in v3. These are results under revised settings, not demonstrated same-setting gains. The original ablation and accepted-token values remain in v3 Tables 4 and 7.

T1.justification: v3 removes v1 Section 4 and Appendix B, including both theorems and their proofs concerning the optimal window size and expected accepted-token count. Window selection becomes an empirical recommendation to round the model-speed ratio. New mathematical arguments concern lossless zero-padding for tensor parallelism and GPU scheduling in Appendices F–G; they do not replace the removed guarantees.

C1.justification: The central parallel-decoding and adaptive-draft claims remain, but v3 withdraws the prominent contribution of theoretically establishing optimal window size and greater expected accepted-token counts from the abstract, introduction, and conclusion. The headline acceleration claims also change from 3.79×/1.52× to 4.43×/1.50× relative to autoregressive decoding/SD.

C2.justification: v1 briefly acknowledges GPU scheduling as a limitation. v3 explicitly distinguishes resource-adequate and co-located deployment, explains resource competition, and discusses the scheduling solution's applicability. It also explains why accepted-token counts alone do not determine speedup and interprets additional forward passes as increased power consumption, without reporting direct energy measurements.

D1.justification: v3 adds a stated code-repository location, MGSM sample counts, Llama 3.1 model specifications, Transformers-version incompatibilities, and explicit information about SD window tuning and separate-device deployment. Appendix G documents draft-model duplication, KV-cache transfer, memory estimates, and NVLink assumptions. Hardware and generation-limit disclosures are also revised.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion or citations for EAGLE, GLIDE, Assisted Generation, newer models, MGSM, and serving systems, including a connection to DistServe's disaggregation approach. The Claude 3 reference is removed. The principal positioning of PEARL as complementary to existing draft-then-verify methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized from theoretical guarantees followed by validation toward empirical evaluation and deployment discussion. The contribution list and standalone Analysis section disappear, case-study explanations are rewritten, and a detailed execution walkthrough replaces the proof appendix. Much of the core methodology prose remains recognizable.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn, and Figure 2(a)'s measured timing bars are replaced by a scheduling schematic. The combined GSM8K/MT-bench table becomes separate language- and category-level displays. New profiling and deployment tables, colored ablation differences, relocated algorithms, and conference formatting substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially addresses v1's untested resource-competition limitation through a concrete scheduling adaptation, transfer-cost measurements, and deployment experiments. Broader language coverage and explicit baseline-tuning information strengthen the empirical basis. Removing the formal guarantees also eliminates v1 Appendix B's erroneous geometric-series evaluation. Reporting ambiguities remain: v3 Table 4 retains old ablation totals despite revised main results, and Table 12 repeats Table 2's SD/PEARL values under a different model label. These weaknesses qualify, but do not outweigh, the substantial gains in practical evidence and transparency.
